description: Track what this add-on bundles: Grafana Alloy, the Home Assistant base image, the GitHub Actions and the Loki used in CI. CONTENT (Alloy, base image digest, CI Loki) automerges once the e2e gate is green - the gate genuinely vets those. The ACTIONS that build and publish are pinned by commit SHA and their bumps stay manual PRs: a compromised action can push a poisoned image under a good tag, and no e2e catches that. A merge publishes an image; Home Assistant installs it through the add-on's auto-update.

customManagers.description: ALLOY_VERSION in the Dockerfile follows grafana/alloy releases

The add-on version IS the Alloy version, so config.yaml moves with the same release. No ^ anchor: without a multiline flag it only matched at file start, and the file starts with a comment - Renovate's first PR bumped the Dockerfile alone. Versioning loose: the file holds <alloy>.<addon-rev>, four components, which semver cannot compare.
alloy-host's version is <base tag>.<host rev>; when the base image tag moves, this moves with it (Renovate writes the plain base tag, host rev restarts at the next host-only change)

packageRules.description: One PR per Alloy release, touching Dockerfile and config.yaml together

Alloy patch and minor releases automerge after the e2e gate, 3 days after release. MAJORS stay manual: strangers' Home Assistants are downstream, and a major can change semantics their own additional_config depends on that the gate never exercises.
Base image tags look like trixie-2026.08.0: track the date part within the trixie line; automerges after the e2e gate rebuilds on it
Pin the builder actions to their release tags, not a floating branch
The CI Loki (a service container in build-app.yaml) is content the gate exercises: automerge, digest-pinned
Actions never automerge; Renovate proposes SHA bumps (with the version in a comment) for a human to read

The host variant is built FROM the published base: tag+digest in its Dockerfile and the version in its config.yaml move together, gated and automerged like content. Loose versioning for the 4-part base tag.
